description: Public prompt text of the certificate condition (DESIGN section 4). The JSON is the single source of truth for every sentence except the per-row question line and the image size. Placeholders: {W} and {H} in frame texts only.

frames.px_source: Image size: {W}x{H} pixels. Give every box as [x0, y0, x1, y1] and every point as [x, y] in pixels of this image (origin at the top-left corner, x to the right, y downward).
frames.rel1000: Give every box as [x0, y0, x1, y1] and every point as [x, y] in coordinates normalized to 0-1000 (0,0 is the top-left corner and 1000,1000 the bottom-right corner).

envelope: End your response with one JSON object with exactly the keys "annotation", "certificate" and "answer". All numbers in "certificate" and "answer" are integers.

task_games__chess__colored_piece_kind_co.annotation_hint: set "annotation" to a JSON array of piece boxes [x0, y0, x1, y1] for every matching visible piece; use an empty array if none are shown
task_games__chess__colored_piece_kind_co.answer_hint: set "answer" to the count of matching visible pieces

task_games__chess__piece_kind_count.annotation_hint: set "annotation" to a JSON array of piece boxes [x0, y0, x1, y1] for every matching visible piece; use an empty array if none are shown
task_games__chess__piece_kind_count.answer_hint: set "answer" to the count of matching visible pieces

selected_set.certificate_line: Certificate format: set "certificate" to {"kind": "selected_set", "members": [...], "count": n} with one member per box in "annotation", in the same order: {"annotation_index": i, "color": c, "piece": p}. Here i is the 0-based position of the box in "annotation", c is "white" or "black", and p is one of "pawn", "knight", "bishop", "rook", "queen" or "king", as seen in that box. n is the number of members. At most 64 members; use "members": [] and "count": 0 if there are none.

task_charts__table__filtered_column_mean.annotation_hint: set "annotation" to an object with "filter_cells" and "target_cells", each mapping to arrays of [x0,y0,x1,y1] boxes for the selected rows
task_charts__table__filtered_column_mean.answer_hint: set "answer" to the exact integer result

filtered_mean.certificate_line: Certificate format: set "certificate" to {"kind": "filtered_mean", "rows": [...], "sum": s, "count": k, "mean": m} with one row per selected row: {"annotation_index": i, "filter_value": f, "target_value": t}. Here i is the 0-based position of the row's boxes in both "filter_cells" and "target_cells" (the two lists must list the rows in the same order), f is the number printed in the row's filter-column cell and t is the number printed in the row's target-column cell. s is the sum of all t, k is the number of rows and m = s / k. At most 16 rows.

task_physics__lever__side_torque_value.annotation_hint: set "annotation" to an array of [x0,y0,x1,y1] boxes around every weight block on the queried side of the fulcrum
task_physics__lever__side_torque_value.answer_hint: set "answer" to the integer torque value

weighted_sum.certificate_line: Certificate format: set "certificate" to {"kind": "weighted_sum", "terms": [...]} with one term per box in "annotation", in the same order: {"annotation_index": i, "weight": w, "distance": d, "product": p}. Here i is the 0-based position of the box in "annotation", w is the number printed on the block, d is the distance mark below the block and p = w × d. At most 8 terms.

task_illustrations__rpg_tactical_map__mo.annotation_hint: set "annotation" to an object with keys "player_cell" and "target_cell", each mapping to one [x0, y0, x1, y1] bounding box around that tile
task_illustrations__rpg_tactical_map__mo.answer_hint: set "answer" to the fewest number of movement points needed to reach the marked target tile

path.certificate_line: Certificate format: set "certificate" to {"kind": "path", "reachable": true, "steps": [...], "total": t}. "steps" lists every tile of a cheapest route from the starting tile to the target tile, in order and including both ends: {"at": [x, y], "cost": c}, where "at" is a point inside the tile and c is the movement cost of entering that tile (0 for the starting tile). t is the sum of all c. Consecutive tiles must be neighbours (up, down, left or right). If the target cannot be reached, use {"kind": "path", "reachable": false}. At most 32 steps.
